title: Cut Credit Exposure or Hedge Rates During a Corporate Bond Drawdown?
grain: One common trading week for four iShares funds
dataset: Issuer historical NAV and ex-dividend distribution records for LQD, IEF, SHY and TLT
question: During a credit drawdown, how does reducing corporate exposure compare with matching its expected rate sensitivity using a Treasury hedge?
design: Form weekly total returns from NAV plus distributions on ex-dates. At each week, use prior returns to estimate rate-factor betas and a lagged drawdown trigger. Compare static credit, a partial move to bills, and a self-financing Treasury overlay at similar expected rate sensitivity. Include costs, turnover, peak-to-trough loss and crisis subperiods.
boundary: A backtest using fund NAVs is a modeled portfolio. Shorting and funding spreads beyond the stated transaction cost can change the comparison. The non-rate residual includes liquidity and issuer-specific risk.
redistribution: Analytical weekly total-return changes only; full issuer workbooks are fetched separately from BlackRock and are not redistributed.

fields.spread_change_bp: Change from preceding month in the Board GZ corporate spread, basis points (descriptive regime only)
fields.rate_change_bp: Change from preceding month in the H.15 ten-year Treasury yield, basis points (descriptive regime only)
